A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain 22 readable pages, including Appendices A–D. Text and visual inspection support a complete comparison; the appendix pages are identical.

before.justification: v2 reports original LLM hierarchy and emotion-recognition experiments, a 60-participant human study, and additional empirical analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the original LLM experiments, 60-participant human study, and appendix results reported in v2.

M1.justification: The matching matrix C = Y^T Y, threshold and asymmetry conditions for hierarchical edges, and extension to general classification tasks remain unchanged (Section 3.1; Appendix B).

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic emotion scenarios, GoEmotions data, wine-aroma scenarios, demographic and intersectional personas, and human emotion-recognition task. Appendix coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: The hierarchical-clustering comparison in Figure 14 and base versus RL-fine-tuned Mistral-7B comparison in Figure 9 retain the same methods. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Both retain 5,000 scenarios for hierarchy extraction, 20 scenarios per emotion for persona evaluation, and 60 human participants. Model configurations, prompts, metrics, and appendix evaluation protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: Prompt-wording robustness, threshold sensitivity, human-hierarchy alignment, persona geometry–accuracy correlations, and demographic misclassification analyses are retained unchanged (Figures 13 and 15–22).

E5.justification: Both retain the same McNemar test, correlation significance reporting, error bars, and plotted uncertainty. No repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty-estimation information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Reported values and graphical findings are unchanged. Both report neutral-persona accuracies of 15.2% over 135 labels and 87.1% over six categories, and Mistral surprise-recognition accuracy of 20.0% for the base model versus 33.3% after RL fine-tuning.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and edge conditions in Section 3.1, probability assumptions and derivations in Appendix A, and general classification formulation in Appendix B are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and Discussion retain the same claims about hierarchical emotion organization with scale, alignment with psychology, demographic biases, and parallels with human judgments.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning emotional granularity, demographic bias, and RL prediction errors are unchanged. Both retain limitations concerning valence/arousal, restricted emotion labels, linguistic proxies, synthetic scenarios, and sociocultural differences.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit code-availability statement and GitHub repository location in the abstract, absent from v2. Other implementation disclosures remain unchanged. The PDFs establish added access information but do not establish repository completeness.

R1.justification: The same-titled EmoBench reference changes attribution from Gurkan et al. to Sabour et al., with revised publication metadata and an added DOI; the duplicate Nielsen author is removed. These are bibliographic edits, with unchanged cited-work coverage and research positioning.

P1.justification: Edits comprise the added code-availability sentence, revised author citations and bibliography metadata, and updated version/date stamp. The remaining prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Body text reflows across columns and pages: Section 3 moves from page 2 to page 3, and Discussion from page 7 to page 8. Figures, tables, and captions retain their presentation; appendix layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: The added project-code location and bibliographic corrections modestly improve reproducibility documentation and reference traceability. Scientific evidence and appendices remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited; code completeness is not established by the PDFs.
